crimes.act: Divulges the contents of any communication (other than one to such person or entity, or an agent thereof) while in transmission on that service to any person or entity other than an addressee or intended recipient of such communication or an agent of such addressee or intended recipient
crimes.who: A person or entity providing an electronic communication service to the public
federalBasis: Electronic communication service to the public
intent: Intentionally

penalties.penalty: Set in another law (no penalty for (3)(a) is stated in this section; (4)(a) penalizes violations of subsection (1) only)

exceptions: The provider may divulge the contents: as otherwise authorized in section 2511(2)(a) or 2517; with the lawful consent of the originator or any addressee or intended recipient; to a person employed or authorized, or whose facilities are used, to forward the communication to its destination; or, if inadvertently obtained by the service provider and appearing to pertain to the commission of a crime, to a law enforcement agency

intent: Intentionally

crimes.act: Sends through the mail, or sends or carries in interstate or foreign commerce, any electronic, mechanical, or other device
ways: sends in interstate or foreign commerce
carries in interstate or foreign commerce
federalBasis: The device is sent through the mail, or sent or carried in interstate or foreign commerce
knowledge: Knowing or having reason to know that the design of such device renders it primarily useful for the purpose of the surreptitious interception of wire, oral, or electronic communications
exceptions: Except as otherwise specifically provided in this chapter

Not unlawful for a provider of wire or electronic communication service or an officer, agent, or employee of, or a person under contract with, such a provider, in the normal course of the business of providing that service
Not unlawful for an officer, agent, or employee of, or a person under contract with, the United States, a State, or a political subdivision thereof, in the normal course of its activities

crimes.act: Manufactures, assembles, possesses, or sells any electronic, mechanical, or other device
federalBasis: The device or any component thereof has been or will be sent through the mail or transported in interstate or foreign commerce
knowledge: Knowing or having reason to know that the design of such device renders it primarily useful for the purpose of the surreptitious interception of wire, oral, or electronic communications
Knowing or having reason to know that such device or any component thereof has been or will be sent through the mail or transported in interstate or foreign commerce
exceptions: Except as otherwise specifically provided in this chapter

Not unlawful for a provider of wire or electronic communication service or an officer, agent, or employee of, or a person under contract with, such a provider, in the normal course of the business of providing that service
Not unlawful for an officer, agent, or employee of, or a person under contract with, the United States, a State, or a political subdivision thereof, in the normal course of its activities

crimes.act: Places in any newspaper, magazine, handbill, or other publication or disseminates by electronic means any advertisement of an electronic, mechanical, or other device
ways: places in any newspaper, magazine, handbill, or other publication
federalBasis: The advertisement will be sent through the mail or transported in interstate or foreign commerce
knowledge: Knowing the content of the advertisement
Knowing or having reason to know that such advertisement will be sent through the mail or transported in interstate or foreign commerce

For a device under (c)(i): knowing or having reason to know that the design of such device renders it primarily useful for the purpose of the surreptitious interception of wire, oral, or electronic communications
conditions: The advertisement is of (i) a device whose design renders it primarily useful for the purpose of surreptitious interception of wire, oral, or electronic communications, or (ii) any other device, where the advertisement promotes its use for the purpose of surreptitious interception of wire, oral, or electronic communications
exceptions: Except as otherwise specifically provided in this chapter

Not unlawful to advertise for sale a device described in (1) if the advertisement is mailed, sent, or carried in interstate or foreign commerce solely to a domestic provider of wire or electronic communication service or to an agency of the United States, a State, or a political subdivision thereof which is duly authorized to use such device

intent: Intentionally
